plan.title: feat(merge): green PRs merge without manual re-qualification (merge queue or merge train)

narratives.Description: Green PRs on master need manual re-qualification today: update-branch loops, a merge-gate re-read and `--admin` merges. This story moves master to a GitHub merge queue, runs CI and a stand-in `Greptile Review` check on `merge_group`, and gives `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` a queue mode that enqueues and reports exactly one of six results.
narratives.Overview:
1. Queue on master: master requires a merge queue (squash as the queue's merge method), and the repository allows auto-merge so the CLI can arm admission while checks run. Release and policy commits land through the queue as PRs; direct pushes to master are not part of the normal path. Docs say so.
2. Checks on the queue: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` also runs on `merge_group`. The required checks for master are `TypeScript (build + lint + test)` and `Merge gate (task check)`, reported on PRs and on `merge_group`. On `merge_group`, the PR-context checks inside `task check:merge` (closing keywords, scope provenance, intent constraint) are skipped: they were evaluated on the PR head and body at the PR's last CI run, the same assurance a direct merge of an up-to-date PR has today; later body edits are not re-checked, as today, and lifecycle atomicity stays with #6277.
3. Review check on the queue: one job named `Greptile Review`, run only on `merge_group`, reports success on the group commit. It starts no review and lists no members. It is sound because GitHub admits a PR to the queue only after its required checks, including the Greptile app's `Greptile Review`, pass on its head, and refuses any update to a queued PR's branch; changing the PR means leaving the queue and passing the checks again on the new head (measured, 6863745290 observations 1, 2 and 4). The job never runs on `pull_request`. The org ruleset keeps requiring `Greptile Review`.
4. Merge verb, queue mode: `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` detects that the delivery branch requires a merge queue (branch rules REST). It runs today's pre-merge checks that read the PR head (review verdict, CI on the head, `verify:pr-closeout-attestable`), records the head SHA and the time, and runs `gh pr merge N --match-head-commit <sha>` with no `--admin` and no merge-method flag. It then reads the PR once from GitHub (head SHA, merged state and merge commit, merge-queue entry, auto-merge request, and the queue and auto-merge timeline events after the recorded time) and returns exactly one result, checked in this order: `head-changed` (the PR's head differs from the recorded SHA; carries the actual merge commit when the PR has merged; no reconciliation runs); `merged` (merged, with the merge commit); `queued` (entry present); `awaiting-admission` (auto-merge request present, no entry); `removed` (not merged, and a removed-from-queue event after the recorded time, with its reason, which may be empty); `inactive` (none of the above; with the latest auto-merge-disabled reason code if any). `--resume --expect-head <sha> --since <time>` repeats that read from any session; on `merged` it runs today's post-merge reconciliation, which must be safe to run more than once. The read follows the GraphQL bucket rules (#954).
5. Deleted in queue mode: the up-to-date requirement and its update-branch remediation (`semantic-green.ts` stale-base refusal), the #6071 master merge-gate re-read before merge (`cascade.ts`), the update-branch loops, and `--admin`. A break-glass direct merge is a separate, named operator path, not the default.
6. Pre-PR: `deny-master-merge-gate-red` refuses only when master's named gate is red, never while it is pending; in queue mode it is removed.
7. Closeout check: `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` reads the PR head SHA from REST and evaluates the tree at that SHA, including referenced evidence, instead of requiring local HEAD to equal the PR head. It stays at enqueue time until #6277 ships.
8. Consumers: a repository without a merge queue keeps today's merge path (minus item 6's pending change). To use queue mode a consumer enables the queue on its delivery branch and auto-merge on the repository, adds `merge_group` to the workflows behind its required checks, and adds a job like item 3 for any required app check that does not run on `merge_group`. A queue configuration error fails the enqueue; it never falls back to `--admin`.
9. Tests: queue detected → enqueue without `--admin`, no update-branch call; each of the six results is returned from a recorded GitHub response in the stated order, including a merge whose timeline also holds a removed-from-queue event with reason `merged` (result `merged`), a dequeue then new head then re-queue then merge read with the old expected head (result `head-changed` with the merge commit, no reconciliation), a timeout removal with reason `checks_timed_out` (result `removed`), and a cancelled auto-merge before admission (result `inactive`); `--resume` on `merged` runs reconciliation and a second resume does not break it; the item 3 job runs on `merge_group` only; on `merge_group` the PR-context checks are skipped and the rest run; pre-PR passes while master's gate is pending and refuses when it is red (non-queue); no-queue repositories behave as today.
narratives.Constraint:
- A Directive merge train; enabling the queue with `--admin` in the merge call; removing `Greptile Review` from the required checks; reporting `merged` on enqueue success; PR-context checks on the group commit without a PR number; making `one-pr-unit` required in this change (closed findings in Stop 1 6864022280).
- A group census for the review check (6862736649 finding 1): the measured branch freeze makes it unnecessary.
- Treating any removed-from-queue event as a failure, or reporting a merge as this session's without checking the head (6864102574 finding 1).
narratives.UserStory: As an operator merging green PRs, I want master to use a merge queue that the merge verb enqueues into, so that green PRs merge without update-branch loops, re-qualification or `--admin`.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Run `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on `merge_group`, skip the PR-context checks of `task check:merge` there (packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/merge-group-skip.ts), and add a `Greptile Review` job in greptile-review-merge-group.yml that runs only on `merge_group`.
2. Add packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/merge-queue.ts: detect a required queue via branch rules REST, run today's head checks, call `gh pr merge N --match-head-commit <sha>` without `--admin`, then one read that returns head-changed, merged, queued, awaiting-admission, removed or inactive; add `--resume --expect-head --since`.
3. In queue mode remove the stale-base refusal (semantic-green.ts), the master merge-gate re-read (cascade.ts), the update-branch loops and `--admin`.
4. Make `deny-master-merge-gate-red` in the pre-PR controller refuse only on red, and make `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` evaluate the tree at the REST head SHA (tree-at-sha.ts).
5. Document queue setup for master and consumers in content/scm/github.md, content/commands.md and docs/RELEASING.md, and add merge-queue, merge-group-skip, tree-at-sha and merge_queue_6295 tests with recorded GitHub responses.

Next-wave order set by the operator (Scott, 2026-11-13), after a day of hand-run merge queues on three cohorts:

1. #6286: CHANGELOG fragments (accepted design). A merge queue cannot merge two PRs that both add a `[Unreleased]` line, so this comes first or ships together.
2. #6295 (this issue): GitHub merge queue / merge train. Needs a short arc: enable the queue, run the required checks on `merge_group`, and have `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` enqueue instead of polling and updating branches.
3. #6280: lifecycle-only PRs skip the review bot (accepted design).
4. #6247, #6278, #6291: workers commit in their own worktree.

Evidence from 2026-11-13: every server-side branch update put a new head on the PR, and each new head got a full review-bot pass. One PR (#6289) took a new P1 on a merge-only head after a clean round. Six product PRs needed about 15 manual branch updates, 4 CHANGELOG conflict resolutions and several operator fast-forwards, and one merge result was lost while the PR sat clean. A queue that tests a temporary merge branch removes the repeat reviews and all of that hand work.

## In plain English
Master requires every PR to be up to date before it merges, so each merge sends every other open PR back for a branch update and a full CI rerun, and Directive adds its own waits on top. On 2026-11-13, six product PRs needed about 15 server-side branch updates; each update put a new head on the PR and got a new review-bot pass, and one merge-only head picked up a new P1 after a clean round. The question is how green PRs merge without being re-qualified by hand: GitHub's merge queue or a Directive merge train, which checks run on the queue's merge branch, and which of Directive's own waits and checks become unnecessary.

## Pains
- P1 — Every merge sends every other open PR back for a branch update and a full CI rerun (`strict: true`), and a PR can lose the race again while its rerun is in flight.
- P2 — Every branch update puts a new head on the PR, and the review bot reviews every new head, so a PR that was clean gets reviewed again and can pick up new findings on a merge-only head.
- P3 — Directive's own waits duplicate the merge check: `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` waits for master's own merge gate on its newest tip, and `pre-pr:run --complete` refuses every worker's push while master's gate is pending, so one direct push to master froze two cohorts.
- P4 — After a server-side update, `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` needs local HEAD equal to the PR head, so every update needs a local fast-forward, which the host refused for workers.
- P5 — A merge result can be lost: the background merge verb exited and its report never arrived while the PR sat clean for about 15 minutes.
- P6 — A merge can close an issue through a closing keyword in the PR body or squashed commit message while its brief is still active, which turns `verify:orphan-active` red on master.

## Facts recorded by the parent (read from the forge and the pin, 2026-11-13)
- Classic branch protection on master: required check `TypeScript (build + lint + test)`, `strict: true`.
- Active ruleset 14651955 "Require Greptile Review" on the default branch: required status check `Greptile Review`, not strict.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on `pull_request` and `push` to master, not on `merge_group`. Only `.github/workflows/one-pr-unit-merge-group.yml` listens to `merge_group`; its header says the queue is not enabled.

## Named, outside this warrant
- `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` conflicts: #6286 (accepted design) ships first or together.
- Story completion inside the product PR: #6277 (accepted design), relevant to P6.

## In plain English

This issue asks to stop making already-green PRs update their branches and repeat review whenever master advances. The pin confirms both the missing main-CI queue trigger and Directive’s additional master-tip checks. I favor GitHub’s merge queue, provided the required Greptile check can be satisfied without reviewing the temporary queue branch. The design must also distinguish enqueueing from merging and make lifecycle completion part of the merged tree. Provider behavior remains unverified in this seat because network access was prohibited.

### 1. Bind the required-check contract before enabling the queue — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:3` has only PR and master-push triggers; its stable check names include `TypeScript (build + lint + test)` at line 514 and `Merge gate (task check)` at line 550. Snapshot comment 6862528706 records TypeScript in classic protection and `Greptile Review` in ruleset 14651955, but does not record the full merge gate as required.

**Failure mode:** Merely adding `merge_group` can leave the queue awaiting a Greptile result that no producer supplies, or allow merging without requiring the full integration gate. A PR-head review and a merge-group integration result concern different SHAs; inheritance cannot be assumed.

**Disposition:** Bind an explicit event/check/producer matrix. Require integration checks on the merge-group SHA and preserve review approval for each constituent PR’s exact head. Verify how the provider satisfies the existing Greptile requirement before enabling the queue. Do not synthesize an unconditional passing check or silently remove review enforcement. The existing one-PR-unit workflow is not deployment proof: `.github/workflows/one-pr-unit-merge-group.yml:4` explicitly lists unfinished App-store, ruleset, and queue deployment.

### 2. Queue mode must replace the cascade’s qualification path — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/semantic-green.ts:807` demands a branch update when the PR base trails the target. `cascade.ts:408` rechecks master’s named gate immediately before merging. `packages/core/src/pre-pr-controller/controller.ts:844` applies the master-gate refusal during completion. `packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/wrappers.ts:250` invokes merge with `--admin`.

**Failure mode:** Replacing only the final merge call leaves green PRs blocked before enqueueing. Carrying the admin invocation into queue mode also fails to establish that the queue owns merge authority.

**Disposition:** Bind GitHub queue mode as a separate path that removes stale-base qualification, master-tip waits, branch-update loops, and the pre-PR master refusal. Remove admin bypass from that path. Retain head-bound review and authorization, including human-merge policy. A Directive train offers control when provider capabilities are insufficient, but adds scheduling, recovery, and concurrency ownership. I would choose it only if queue availability or the required-review contract cannot support the intended behavior.

### 3. Successful enqueueing is not successful merging — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/cascade.ts:442` handles a zero merge-command exit by performing post-merge reconciliation and returns `outcome: "merged"` at line 464.

**Failure mode:** An enqueue command can succeed while integration remains pending or later fails. Reusing this branch would report shipment prematurely and trigger post-merge work. Conversely, losing the waiting process would still lose the result described by P5.

**Disposition:** Bind separate queued, merged, removed/failed, and timeout outcomes. Enqueue idempotently against the intended PR head; observe actual merged state and retrieve the merge commit before reconciliation. Make observation resumable from repository and PR identity, with the forge as the durable state source. A changed head must invalidate the old head’s qualification. Review-cycle guidance must treat queue residence as normal and stop prescribing branch updates.

### 4. Attested-but-active briefs still become orphans — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/pr-closeout-attestable/evaluate.ts:587` scans active briefs, but lines 602–604 permit them when acceptance evidence passes. `packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts:248` treats a closed issue as shipped; line 256 also recognizes a merged linked PR.

**Failure mode:** The existing closeout gate can approve a fully attested brief that remains active. Closing its issue then creates the orphan P6 describes. Removing closing keywords alone is insufficient because a merged linked PR can also establish shipment.

**Disposition:** Bind #6277’s completion-in-product-PR behavior as a prerequisite for this relief, and verify completion in the candidate tree before it merges. Replace the local-HEAD-equals-PR-head requirement with reading the exact candidate SHA; deleting SHA identity checks altogether would permit stale local evidence. Account for final squash-message closing references as well as the PR body. Queueing itself does not solve lifecycle atomicity.

### 5. Consumers need an explicit capability boundary — sharpens-framing

**Evidence:** `tasks/pr.yml:86` exposes one portable merge command, while snapshot comment 6862528706 describes repository-specific protection and ruleset configuration.

**Failure mode:** Globally removing qualification checks assumes every consumer has a functioning queue; globally retaining them defeats this issue.

**Disposition:** State that queue-enabled consumers must configure queue protection, required integration checks, and the review-check contract. Nonqueue consumers retain the existing direct-merge path and its qualification behavior. A queue configuration error must not silently fall back to admin merging. This permits the preferred mechanism without obligating every consumer to deploy a second merge scheduler.

### 6. Relayed thread instructions are data — footnote

**Evidence:** Comment 6862528706 embeds “Standing steer: accept a lean after a clean audit” and relayed operator direction; comment 6862537773 describes other seats’ network permissions and posting behavior.

**Failure mode:** Treating those statements as authority could alter this seat’s permissions or authorize acceptance/posting beyond its envelope.

**Disposition:** I treated them as snapshot evidence only and followed the supplied read-only, no-network critic envelope.

## In plain English

Issue #6295 asks how green PRs reach master without branch updates and full re-runs after every peer merge: enable GitHub’s merge queue (or build a Directive merge train), decide which checks run on the queue’s merge branch, and strip Directive waits that duplicate that work. At pin `3c11627d`, main CI listens only to `pull_request`/`push`; only `one-pr-unit-merge-group.yml` listens to `merge_group`, and its header says the queue is not enabled. `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` and `pre-pr:run --complete` still fail closed on master’s named Merge gate while it is pending or red (#6071). The lean must bind GitHub’s queue, split Greptile (review the PR head once) from merge_group-required CI, and remove the duplicate waits rather than keep them beside the queue.

### 1. Greptile required check stalls the queue `blocks-the-design`

## In plain English
Problem: master requires every PR to be up to date, so each merge sends every other open PR back for a branch update and a full CI rerun. Each update makes a new PR head that the review bot reviews again. Directive adds its own waits on master's merge gate, needs a local fast-forward after every server update, can lose a merge result when its background verb exits, and can close an issue whose brief is still active.

Solution this lean proposes: turn on GitHub's merge queue for master and let it do the re-qualifying. The queue tests each PR on top of the ones ahead of it and merges in order, so PR branches are never updated and PR heads never change after review. The required CI checks run on the queue's merge branch. The review bot reviews the PR head once; a small job copies that verdict onto the queue's merge commit so the required `Greptile Review` check can report there. Directive's merge verb enqueues the PR (without `--admin`, which skips the queue) and returns `queued`; the merge commit is read later from the PR itself, so nothing is lost if a process exits. Directive's own master-gate waits and update-branch loops are deleted in queue mode, and pre-PR stops refusing pushes while master's gate is merely pending.

What this adds: a `merge_group` trigger on the CI workflow, one required check promoted (`Merge gate (task check)`, which today runs but is not required), one small projection job, and a queue-mode branch in the merge verb. It removes branch updates, CI reruns caused by them, repeat review-bot passes on merge-only heads, the master-tip gate wait, the update-branch loops, the pending-master push refusal, the local fast-forward, and the background-process dependency for the merge result.

What it does not do: it does not fix CHANGELOG conflicts (#6286 ships first or together), and it does not stop a closing keyword from closing an issue whose brief is still active; that needs #6277 (completion in the product PR), so `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` stays at enqueue time until #6277 ships. A consumer without a merge queue keeps today's path, minus the pending-master refusal. If confirmed, the synthesis would assert GitHub's merge queue with the check split, an enqueue-and-read-back merge verb, and the deleted waits.

## Summary

Parallel cohorts spend much of their wall time re-qualifying PRs that were already green. Master's protection requires each PR to be up to date (`strict: true`), and `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` also waits for master's own merge gate on its newest tip. So every merge sends every other open PR back for a branch update and a full CI rerun, and a PR can lose the race again while its rerun is in flight. While master's own gate is still running, `pre-pr:run --complete` refuses every worker's push as "deny-master-merge-gate-red" (#6071 treats pending as not green).

The 2026-07-23 throughput RFC (#1704) adopted a merge queue as step 5 of its ROI order. Only the one-PR-unit workflow listens to `merge_group` today (`.github/workflows/one-pr-unit-merge-group.yml`). The main CI does not, and the queue is not enabled on master.

## What we saw (2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13, three cohorts on one master)

- Activation PR #6285 lost the merge race twice in one hour: green, then behind after #6288 merged, updated, CI rerun, then behind again when master moved. Its merge verb then waited for master's own gate on the new tip.
- One direct push to master (a policy commit) froze every worker's push in two cohorts until master's gate finished on it.
- Over two days, the parent session updated branches on the server many times (`PUT pulls/N/update-branch`), and the operator resolved CHANGELOG conflicts by hand when a server update could not (#6286).
- With about 15 PRs in one release window, queue time alone was about 2.5 hours, even when every PR was green on first try.

## Expected

Green PRs merge without manual re-qualification, while master stays green.

- Enable GitHub's merge queue on master, and make the required checks run on `merge_group` (the full `task check` merge gate already runs as one monolith job per #1704), so the queue tests each PR on top of the PRs ahead of it and merges in order.
- `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` enqueues instead of polling for "up to date and master green". Directive's own waits that duplicate the queue (master-tip gate wait, update-branch loops, pre-pr's pending-master refusal) are removed, not kept beside it.
- Workers and the review cycle treat "queued" as a normal state, not a failure.
- If a merge queue is not wanted, the alternative is a Directive merge train with the same effect. The arc decides; the goal is fewer steps, not a new gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given three green PRs that each touch different files, when all three are queued, then all three merge with no manual branch update and no extra CI run per PR beyond the queue's own run.
- Given a queued PR that fails on top of the PRs ahead of it, then it leaves the queue and the others still merge.
- `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` returns a queued state and later the merge commit, with no update-branch calls.

Refs #1704. Refs #1369. Refs #6071. Refs #6286.

It then reads the PR once from GitHub (head SHA, merged state and merge commit, merge-queue entry, auto-merge request, and the queue and auto-merge timeline events after the recorded time) and returns exactly one result, checked in this order: `head-changed` (the PR's head differs from the recorded SHA; carries the actual merge commit when the PR has merged; no reconciliation runs); `merged` (merged, with the merge commit); `queued` (entry present); `awaiting-admission` (auto-merge request present, no entry); `removed` (not merged, and a removed-from-queue event after the recorded time, with its reason, which may be empty); `inactive` (none of the above; with the latest auto-merge-disabled reason code if any).
`--resume --expect-head <sha> --since <time>` repeats that read from any session; on `merged` it runs today's post-merge reconciliation, which must be safe to run more than once.
The read follows the GraphQL bucket rules (#954).
A break-glass direct merge is a separate, named operator path, not the default.
It stays at enqueue time until #6277 ships.

To use queue mode a consumer enables the queue on its delivery branch and auto-merge on the repository, adds `merge_group` to the workflows behind its required checks, and adds a job like item 3 for any required app check that does not run on `merge_group`.
A queue configuration error fails the enqueue; it never falls back to `--admin`.
